claims.text: Cyclic mechanical wear at elevated temperature removes or disrupts protective oxide films along phase boundaries.
Oxide disruption exposes interfaces between relatively noble and corrosion-sensitive phases.
The exposed dissimilar phases form micro-galvanic couples.
Micro-galvanic coupling accelerates localized corrosion at interphase interfaces.
Localized corrosion weakens phase boundaries.
Corrosion-weakened interfaces are more susceptible to subsequent mechanical removal and abrasion.
The reciprocal enhancement of corrosion and wear creates a positive feedback loop that accelerates overall degradation.
AlCoCrFeNi-type eutectic high-entropy alloys can have a dual-phase microstructure.
The target microstructure contains a noble FCC or ordered-B2 phase and a less noble BCC phase.
A stable protective oxide film is initially present along the phase boundaries.
The proposed comparison uses simultaneous wear-corrosion, inert-atmosphere wear-only, and static corrosion-only conditions.
AlCoCrFeNi-family alloys exhibit measurable elevated-temperature wear and hot-salt corrosion responses, although the cited studies evaluate these responses separately.
Approximately 800 degrees Celsius in an oxidizing or reactive-salt environment is an applicable condition for the proposed coupled mechanism.
Total degradation under simultaneous wear and corrosion will exceed the sum of degradation measured under isolated wear and isolated corrosion.
Wear-track depth will be greater in the coupled test than in the matched wear-only test.
Corrosion-related mass loss will be greater in the coupled test than in the matched corrosion-only test.
The mechanism applies when a normally stable oxide is mechanically disrupted while corrosive species and mechanical loading are simultaneously active.
The magnitude of synergy depends on phase distribution, oxide integrity, mechanical load, and environmental aggressiveness.
Wear depth and gravimetric mass loss provide measurable responses, but the proposed gravimetric measurement alone does not isolate corrosion loss from wear loss during the coupled test.
Failure to observe superadditive degradation or localized micro-galvanic attack at phase boundaries is designated as a falsifying result.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires total coupled degradation to exceed the sum of isolated losses while each component merely increases relative to its corresponding isolated control. The falsification rule instead appears to require both wear and corrosion mass loss individually to exceed the sum of the two isolated effects, which is a different and dimensionally ambiguous criterion.
